question: Which discovery method gives the most relevant, embeddable, popular YouTube videos per dish at an acceptable cost, without using the YouTube search quota?

methods.A: YouTube search.list (order=relevance, 25 results, query '<dish> 레시피'), then videos.list; keep embeddable public videos whose title contains the dish name; top 3 by views.
methods.B: OpenRouter google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite:online asked for YouTube watch URLs for '<dish> 레시피'; ids from the answer text and url citations; one batched videos.list verifies them; same filter and ranking as A.
methods.C: B plus a second query '<dish> 만들기' to the same model; ids merged; one batched videos.list; same filter and ranking.

sample.rule: 10 dishes already cached for method A, plus 30 drawn per category (largest-remainder quotas over the other dishes, random.Random(seed).sample, then shuffled with the same generator); see sampling.py

normalisation: lower-case, keep letters and digits only (so spaces and punctuation are ignored)

metrics.relevance_strict: verified embeddable candidates whose normalised title contains the normalised dish name / all verified embeddable candidates, pooled over dishes
metrics.relevance_loose: the same with the dish name or any alias
metrics.embeddable_share: verified existing videos that are embeddable and public / verified existing videos (before the filter); kept videos are 100% by construction
metrics.existence_rate: ids returned by videos.list / distinct ids extracted from the model answer (B, C)
metrics.coverage: dishes with 3 kept videos (title names the dish) / dishes with a run of that method
metrics.median_views: median view count of kept videos
metrics.cost: OpenRouter-reported USD per dish; YouTube quota units (search.list 100 in its own bucket of about 100 calls per day, videos.list 1)
metrics.latency: median wall seconds per discovery call

method_a_notes: The 10 cached dishes reuse the stored top 3 of an earlier run (no new search call). Those 3 are the most viewed named videos filled up with relevance order, so coverage is exact for them (3 named videos stored means 3 exist) but candidate relevance is not comparable and is excluded from relevance_strict of A.
Relevance and the decision rule compare methods on the dishes where A ran live (paired); coverage compares on all dishes where A has a result.
A runs live on at most 20 dishes with at most 25 extra search.list calls; the rest are reported as pending.
no_human_check: Relevance is a title string match, not a human judgement; a title can name the dish and still be a poor recipe video, or omit the name and be a good one.
